ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the die is located at the left-side starting point A, and it can be seen that the top face has 3 dots, the front face has 2 dots, and the right face has 1 dot. The directions of the grid route from A to B are, in order: rightward, rightward, downward, downward, rightward, rightward, rightward. Reasoning: The sums of dots on opposite faces of a die are 7, so initially the bottom face opposite the top face 3 is 4, the back face opposite the front face 2 is 5, and the left face opposite the right face 1 is 6. The initial position is: top=3, bottom=4, front=2, back=5, right=1, left=6. Roll rightward once, the left face goes to the top, top=6; roll rightward once again, the left face goes to the top, top=4. Roll downward/forward once, the back face goes to the top, top=5; roll downward/forward once again, the back face goes to the top, top=3. After that, roll rightward three times continuously: the first time top=1, the second time top=4, the third time top=6. Therefore, when it reaches B, the top face is 6.

method.method_draft: Read the die and route from the image: at A the visible faces show top = 3, front = 2, right side = 1, and the path requires rolls right, right, down, down, right, right, right to reach B. From the text use the rule that opposite faces sum to 7, so bottom = 4, back = 5, left = 6. Then simulate each roll by updating the face positions: a right roll brings the left face to the top, and a down/forward roll brings the back face to the top. After applying the seven rolls in the visual order, the top face at B is 6.
